o1
A bridge in Boston carries 61,200 cars every day.
o2
It stands on foundations nobody can see.
p1
Across Massachusetts, 778 bridges need underwater inspection.
p2
123 of them are scour critical. Together they carry 1.6 million vehicles a day.
p3
To inspect them, MassDOT has 7 full-time divers.
p4
One dive-team day costs 6.8 to 10.8 thousand dollars per bridge.
p5
And scour matters most during floods, exactly when the current is too strong for anyone to dive.
i1
Federal guidance has long said sonar can only supplement divers, not replace them.
i2
A federal dam inspector told us this week: send an ROV down for a visual of the whole basin, then send divers for spot checks.
i3
So divers stay. The robot goes first. Divers only where the map says.
s1
To prove it, we built the whole simulation from scratch after the challenge dropped this morning, in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, a robotics simulator with real-time ray tracing and physics.
s2
We rebuilt the Charles River Dam crossing as a digital twin, from the federal record and photographs.
s3
Inside it run the real ArduPilot autopilots: one flies the drone through a 38-item mission, the other drives the ROV, all talking over ROS 2.
d1
A drone works above the water, carrying 3D lidar, a gimbal camera, simulated thermal, and floodlights.
d2
As it drops below the deck, its GPS fix falls from 12 satellites to 7.
d3
It maps the structure and flags defects right down to the water line.
r1
Below the surface, an ROV takes over, where there is no GPS at all.
r2
It navigates on a Doppler velocity log, drifting only about 0.4 meters over 60 meters.
r3
Multibeam sonar lets it see through dark water the drone can never reach.
t1
At the water line, the two robots hand off.
t2
The drone flagged 4 defects; the ROV dove and inspected all 4 in our recorded run.
t3
The result is one 3D model: 2.96 million lidar points above, 1.58 million sonar points below.
k1
The intelligence was built with Kiro, AWS's agentic AI coding environment.
k2
Megha used Kiro to build the whole detection pipeline and the inspector dashboard.
k3
It runs a YOLOv8 segmentation model on the imagery, retraces each hit into the lidar, and assigns severity by rules.
k4
A report agent must cite a detection for every claim, and a professional engineer signs off.
k5
With Kiro we also built a triage of all 5,252 Massachusetts bridges. Its number one is the North Washington Street bridge, a mile from our site.
m1
Now the money. Today, every bridge gets a full dive-team day.
m2
Robot first, then a targeted dive, runs about 20 to 30 percent less, our estimate, which the pilot will measure.
m3
Our kit lists at 16,448 dollars, against sonar systems that cost 35 to 385 thousand for the sonar alone.
w1
The timing is now. By 15 March 2028, every state must re-code its bridge data, including scour.
w2
Pilot money already exists, through federal STIC and AID Demonstration programs.
w3
New Hampshire is already running an ROV study of its own.
c1
Next is a 10-bridge pilot, every robot map checked against a diver.
c2
Robot first. Divers only where the map says.
